People act like cooking is this giant chore. It's a little bit of prep and a lot of reward after. I generally cook lunch and dinner for the entire week in my pressure/slow cooker on Sundays. This week I tried a new recipe after a voater posted some.

https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/slow-cooker-chicken-taco-salad

The hardest part is mixing the spices and the chicken can be used in just about everything. I can't seem to sleep tonight but since I've decided I like the recipe I'm going ahead and premixing 20 plastic bags w/ the seasoning mix that I'll put in my pantry. I number my recipe and add a (x 2,3,4 etc) to note how many times I've doubled the recipe so I know how much chicken or whatever to add. My favorite recipes are numbered in a binder that match the spice bags. I've got premixed seasoning for about ten recipes I like on my shelves right now. When I want to cook my meat staples for the week I simply add whatever broth and grab my premixed seasoning. It saves a fuckton of time. Also always buy the spices you use a lot of in bulk. One simple investment of time and money upfront can save you countless time throughout the year and keep you from eating crap b/c you're "too tired to cook". When I'm too tired to cook I simply toss a bag of broccoli in the microwave and grab whatever meats I cooked on Sunday from the fridge. The only thing I actually cook every day is eggs and bacon in the morning. That's a sacred part of me waking up. I don't mess w/ that.

It's such a little thing that turns into huge rewards. I've got time to exercise everyday b/c I'm not thinking about what I'm going to eat or taking excess time to prepare it. I just turn on the tv, hop on the treadmill/lift for an hour - hour and a 1/2. I save a ton of money on food as well. It really cuts down on daily stress and gives me more time for family as well. All in all, cooking for the week has made me a better person b/c of the possibilities it opens up. And like I said, premix the spices and even cooking on Sunday isn't a big ordeal. You just toss the shit in the pot and come back sometime later. Easy peasy.

There's a thousand ways to simplify your life.

It goes beyond just that though. I prefer iced coffee so I brew a couple pots at a time for the week and just refrigerate it. I'll also mix up a couple pitchers of crystal light or whatever for the week. It's this little shit that actually gives me time to feel like I'm living my life every week instead of just going through motions.
